source_name: EBRD Procurement Notices (corporate landing / redirect layer)
why_relevant: Explains the split between client procurement (ECEPP) and EBRD's own corporate/consultancy procurement (SMART by GEP), and hosts procurement policy and rules. Needed to know which channel a given Montenegro financial-sector assignment will appear on.

source_name: EBRD corporate consultancy opportunities via SMART by GEP
why_relevant: EBRD-funded advisory and technical-cooperation assignments (financial-sector policy, digital finance, payments diagnostics) contracted by the Bank itself rather than by a client are advertised here, not on ECEPP. These are exactly the small advisory contracts that precede larger Montenegro payments investments.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — procurement notices and contract details
why_relevant: Publishes General Procurement Notices, Specific Procurement Notices, REOIs and contract-award details (fed from STEP) for Bank-financed Montenegro operations, including the EUR 8m Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA TIPS-clone project. This is the single most on-target donor channel for Montenegro payments-infrastructure procurement.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA (TIPS Clone) project documents
why_relevant: Project Appraisal Document (Report No. PADHI01235) for the flagship Montenegro payments project; contains the procurement plan summary, components, implementing agency (Central Bank of Montenegro / Ministry of Finance) and indicative contract packages for the TIPS-clone instant-payment build. Directly names what will be tendered.

source_name: World Bank Group Finances One — contract awards datasets
why_relevant: Machine-readable historical contract-award data by supplier country, procurement method and fiscal year. Lets you see which vendors actually won Bank-financed contracts in Montenegro — competitor and price benchmarking rather than opportunity spotting.

source_name: World Bank corporate procurement contract awards
why_relevant: Bank's own (non-borrower) purchases of advisory and IT services; occasionally covers Western Balkans payments diagnostics and financial-inclusion studies that shape later lending. Secondary but cheap to monitor.

source_name: UNDP Procurement Notices — Montenegro country feed
why_relevant: UNDP Montenegro implements EU-funded digital-government and e-services projects (e.g. the EU/UNDP e-services and digital infrastructure programme with the Ministry of Public Administration) and tenders hardware, software and digital-expert consultancies under its own rules. A country-scoped RSS feed makes this the cheapest high-signal donor feed in the cell.

source_name: UNGM — United Nations Global Marketplace public notices
why_relevant: System-wide UN tender board covering UNDP, UNICEF, UNOPS, IOM etc.; catches Montenegro assignments (e.g. 'Digital Expert' roles) that never reach national channels. Also carries contract-award archives useful for competitor mapping.

source_name: EIB — procurement for Bank-financed projects and technical assistance calls
why_relevant: EIB requires promoters to publish notices in OJEU and/or on eib.org for non-EU projects; Montenegro entries are demonstrably present (railway tunnels, PIU support for the Montenegro Education Programme). PIU-support and technical-assistance calls are the template under which financial-management/payment-system TA would be tendered if EIB co-finances it.

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore — EU fondovi / Direktorat za ugovaranje i finansiranje sredstava EU pomoći (CFCU)
why_relevant: Montenegro's CFCU is the national contracting authority for IPA operational programmes under indirect management: it prepares, concludes and monitors EU-funded contracts. Notices and award information for IPA contracts run through this directorate, in Montenegrin, and it is the actor to name-map when reading TED notices with a Montenegrin contracting authority.

source_name: Revizorsko tijelo Crne Gore (Audit Authority for EU funds) — IPA section
why_relevant: Audits IPA-funded procurement in Montenegro. Audit reports reveal which contracts were actually signed and executed, where procedures failed, and which bodies mismanage donor tenders — high-value indirect intelligence not obtainable from notice feeds.

source_name: KfW Development Bank — procurement guidelines and financed-project tenders
why_relevant: KfW finances Western Balkans financial-sector and SME-finance operations; procurement is run by the borrower under KfW's own Guidelines for Procurement, so notices scatter across borrower websites and aggregators rather than a single KfW board. Montenegro-located tender openings under KfW financing do occur (e.g. a WB6 Chamber Investment Forum tender opened in Podgorica). Track the guidelines to know where notices must land, and monitor borrower sites.

source_name: dgMarket — aggregated donor tender notices
why_relevant: Cross-donor aggregator carrying World Bank, EU, UN and national donor notices in one place. Useful as a recall safety net and for retrospective searching when a donor portal has poor archives; not authoritative and partly paywalled, so treat as secondary.

source_name: CKB banka (Crnogorska komercijalna banka, OTP Group) – corporate site / About us and news sections
why_relevant: Largest bank in Montenegro and the biggest single private buyer of core banking, card, ATM, POS and digital-channel technology in the country. Any occasional public RFP, supplier notice or vendor-partnership announcement would surface on its own site. No dedicated procurement/supplier page was observed in search results; the site must be monitored structurally (news/press) rather than via a procurement feed.

source_name: NLB Banka AD Podgorica – corporate website (O nama / Novosti / Karijera)
why_relevant: Top-3 Montenegrin bank, part of NLB Group; ATM fleet, card and digital-channel spend. Fetched successfully: the site has About Us, News, Careers and Contact but NO procurement, tender, supplier or 'poziv za ponude' section. Confirms that vendor sourcing at NLB ME is centralised/opaque and must be tracked via news, group-level announcements and vendor-side press.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka AD Podgorica – Novosti (news) and Izvještaji (reports) sections
why_relevant: 2nd largest bank in Montenegro by market share (~14.8% per 2025 reporting seen in search snippets). Site structure was retrieved: it has Novosti, Izvještaji, Preuzmite dokumenta and O banci, but explicitly NO procurement/tender/supplier section. Reports and news are therefore the realistic route to vendor and technology-project signals.

source_name: Erste Bank AD Podgorica – corporate website (Novosti)
why_relevant: Systemic Montenegrin bank in Erste Group; significant card/POS/digital spend. Home page was retrieved and shows a Novosti section but no procurement, tender or supplier pages. Group-level Erste procurement policy is the likely governing layer.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore – Saopštenja (corporate announcements) page
why_relevant: Prva banka publishes formal 'javni poziv' notices on its own site — a confirmed detail page for a public call (share issue) was found at /saopstenja_detalji.php?id=148. This proves the bank uses a structured announcements channel where a procurement or vendor-related 'javni poziv' could also appear. Most of the observed calls are capital-markets calls (shares, subordinated bonds), not procurement, so relevance to A2 is indirect but the channel is real and machine-parsable.

source_name: Zapad banka AD Podgorica – corporate website
why_relevant: Smaller Montenegrin bank; smaller banks are the most likely to run an open 'poziv za dostavljanje ponuda' for IT/ATM/card services because they lack an in-house sourcing function. Appeared as a top hit on the local-language phrase search for 'poziv za dostavljanje ponuda' + banka + Crna Gora, which suggests the phrase occurs somewhere on the domain.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD – corporate website and document library
source_subtype: commercial bank corporate website / document repository
why_relevant: Turkish-owned Montenegrin bank; its document library is publicly served (a PDF of e-banking general terms was returned directly by search), meaning the /Documents/ tree is crawlable and may also carry notices, tender or supplier documents. Turkish parent-group sourcing may pull in different vendor names than the EU-group banks — useful for competitor mapping.

source_name: Universal Capital Bank AD Podgorica – corporate website
why_relevant: One of the 11 UBCG member banks; independent (no foreign banking group), so it procures its own core banking, card processing and ATM/POS services locally — a high-value private-buyer target for A2. Named in the cell scope.

source_name: Adriatic Bank AD Podgorica – corporate website
why_relevant: Independent Montenegrin bank named in the cell scope; independent banks buy their technology stack directly and are the most addressable private buyers for payments vendors. No procurement page confirmed in this run.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica – corporate website
why_relevant: Domestic bank named in the cell scope; same rationale as other independents — direct sourcing of core banking/cards/ATM. Not confirmed in this run.
